This little plot near the house is only a small piece, but maize is what feeds my children, so I must care for it well. I keep some chickens and a few goats, so I will carry their manure to the plot before the rains come strong. If my FISP coupon comes this year I will buy a small bag of NPK and some urea — on such a small plot even one bag goes far — but if the coupon does not come I will only manage manure. I am intercropping with pigeon pea as we always do here in Chiradzulu, because the land is small and we must get more than one food from it. I cannot afford pesticides, and there is no irrigation here — we wait for the rains.
